policy: Only validated complete measurement results whose complete benchmark input fingerprint matches may be reused. Eligible units are certified independently after their own validator passes, so a partial run can preserve completed work. Primary configuration is evaluation-scoped: an evaluation sees and hashes shared Primary policy plus only its own evaluation-local section, so changing Proficiency does not re-key Learnability, Language Quality, Semantic Compression, or Ecosystem. Units that measure Quidra are cacheable too: their historical key still carries the declared versions and exact Task Packet, while a separate trusted execution-identity check covers the actual compiler/runtime inputs. This preserves already-paid records without allowing same-version implementation changes to reuse stale results. Cache material is trusted runner input and is never exposed as a worker read path. The three Language Quality mechanical units (the micro suite, the adversarial set and the audit of the snapshot's Quidra programs) are certified too: no model is involved, so their key carries the pinned toolchains of every language they measure, the programs and fixtures they read, the measurement scripts, the snapshot's Quidra versions and a declared mechanical epoch; the raw samples stay in the run's retained artifact.

reuse_conditions.scored_output_cap: The output cap of a scored trial is not part of the key. A certified llm_learnability or llm_proficiency record carries what its trials did against the cap they ran under (scored_output_cap, trial_calls, cap_truncated_trial_calls, max_trial_output_tokens, written at promotion or by cache-annotate-caps from the run's retained agent traces). Under the same cap the record is reused. Under a different cap it is reused only when the cap demonstrably never mattered: no trial call was cut off and no completion was larger than the current cap. A record without this evidence is a MISS until it is annotated.
reuse_conditions.quidra_execution_identity: The historical fingerprint remains unchanged so already-paid cache stays addressable. Reuse of any record that measures Quidra additionally requires an exact compiler/runtime execution identity. New records carry it explicitly; legacy records are accepted only from verified migration commits while the target still equals the frozen migration baseline.
reuse_conditions.same_result_metadata_refresh: When reuse is rejected and a unit is freshly remeasured, identical result bytes do not preserve stale compatibility/certification metadata. The current trust metadata replaces the old record so changed Quidra execution identity or stronger certification cannot create a permanent MISS loop.
reuse_conditions.legacy_identity_ratchet: A verified legacy Quidra record that predates explicit execution identity may be rewritten at checkpoint with the current proven-equivalent execution identity while preserving its historical fingerprint and result. This is counted as an upgrade, not a remeasurement or replacement.
reuse_conditions.ecosystem_runner_rubric: Ecosystem cache reuse requires the same frozen rubric asset through the rendered Task Packet/readable-input hashes and the declared Ecosystem epoch. Pre-v2 language-local rubric results are preserved but are not reused as scored evidence.
reuse_conditions.evaluation_scoped_primary_config: Primary Task Packets and cache keys include shared Primary policy plus only the current evaluation's local section. Historical records created before this scoping migration may be reused only when every non-Primary prompt component and every other fingerprint dependency still match exactly, and the historical full Primary JSON projects to the same current evaluation-specific configuration. A compatible hit is revalidated by the current validator and ratcheted to the current scoped fingerprint at checkpoint; disagreeing compatible records are not reused.

declared_epochs.note: Set by a person, like a toolchain pin. Ecosystem measures external packages, tools and public knowledge, which change independently of language versions. The runner-rubric-v2 epoch deliberately invalidates older Ecosystem score records because they were produced by language-local rubrics; the old records remain preserved in Git but are not score-compatible with the frozen runner-owned rubric contract.
declared_epochs.mechanical_note: Mechanical measurements are timed on the hosted runner class the workflow names. Change this value when that class changes or when the numbers should be taken again for another reason; nothing else about the runner enters the key.
declared_epochs.semantic_compression_note: Semantic Compression v6 preserves the mechanically verified canonical-fragment, trusted-runtime, machine-enforced R9, and comparability-certified cache contracts, and additionally checks frozen exact stdout oracles for every probe whose canonical task fixes a language-neutral concrete result. The runner checks those outputs during the real frozen-recipe execution and rechecks the preserved evidence before downstream scoring. Earlier Semantic Compression records remain preserved but cannot hydrate a v6 run.
declared_epochs.llm_proficiency_note: LLM Proficiency v6 preserves the v5 exact Primary trials, prompt variants, trusted runtime verification, and hidden-input correctness scoring. Hidden oracle cases are now strictly score-only holdout evidence: repair continuation and model-visible feedback depend only on compilation and public cases, so hidden pass/fail information cannot act as an adaptive black-box repair oracle. Earlier Proficiency records remain preserved but cannot hydrate v6.

quidra_execution_identity.purpose: Prevent stale same-version Quidra cache reuse without making benchmark-only commits cold. init records these Git object IDs before .git is excluded from the scored snapshot. New Quidra cache records certify that identity outside the historical fingerprint so existing valid records keep their paths.
quidra_execution_identity.legacy_note: Only legacy records from the listed source commits may use the baseline. Their Quidra execution inputs were verified to equal this map. 56f2c65 is intentionally excluded because its compiler/runtime inputs differ. Once the current target changes, every identity-less legacy Quidra record becomes a MISS even if project.toml keeps the same version.
